Solar Robot Toys 6 in 1 STEM Learning Kits Educational Space Moon Exploration Fleet Building Experiment Toys DIY Solar Power Science Gift for Kids Aged 8-12 [[VIDEOID:4004d9b29ba41ab103b84f18fda795c5]] First off, I have to say the manufacturer is awesome. When I opened the kit it did not have any instructions. Within five hours of first contacting them they sent me a PDF file of the manual. Good on them!

So far, I've made the two types of dogs (it's a head swap, really) and it works really well. Instructions are easy to follow and the pieces fit together easily. This would probably be a good kit for children ages eight and up..if they're a good reader, probably younger would do fine. The only fiddly bits are when you have to take the main modules apart (gear box or battery pack) because they require some firm squeezing that little hands would need assistance with.

The kit uses three different power methods: battery pack, capacitor, and solar power. I tried all three and they each worked just fine. Of course the capacitor worked better than solar, and the battery pack absolutely demolished the others in terms of performance. If the model can support it, I would likely use the capacitor for most things. It is very easy to recharge using the battery pack as well.

I can't wait to put together some of the other bots with my youngest. He's a big fan of building things. Thumbs up!
text_fidelity_b: Solar Robot Toys 6 in 1 STEM Learning Kits Educational Space Moon Exploration Fleet Building Experiment Toys DIY Solar Power Science Gift for Kids Aged 8-12

text_fidelity_a:
Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers I absolutely love the concept of this little worker placement game, but the execution is not great.

You spend each turn doing basic worker placement stuff - go here, get resources, then convert those resources somewhere else, all while building a cell wall around your plant cell in an effort to turn your stuff into points. There is real science here - you use different cell components according to the actual chemical formulas of 6 water + 6CO2 to do photosynthesis, and cards are named after actual scientific stuff. There's also an area control segment of the board where you can earn some minor points and bonuses. The highlight, though, is that when you play this game, you'll know more about real-life science than when you started, and that's a pretty cool thing.

The game suffers though, because there just isn't much to do at the end of the game, and catching up is extremely difficult given that so few actions lead to points, and so many of the things you can collect are useful for only one or two functions. It's a little bit like saying that the science got in the way of the fun. When one person does the action to trigger the end of the game, there is usually a rush to do the singular action left that can generate points, and if you don't have it, you just stockpile some useless resources. That's a poor endgame, and on second or third playthoughs, you'll find that there are really only one or two viable strategies for winning at all.

Ultimately, this is an awesome game for teaching a small group of teenage scientists more about cell structures, but at the price of a hobby board game, it's tough to put in the hands of teachers for classroom use, and harder still to spend valuable class time to educate non-gamers about the intricacies of worker placement prior to their first play. And that play will run the course of a class period, more or less, so that has it's benefits, and it's detriments.

As a gamer's game, we found the concept extremely interesting, but the execution needed a little work. It won't hit the table often, because every other worker placement game we have is more exciting at the endgame, and offers us a greater variety of strategies for winning.

Do note that the addition of the "Mangrove" board, which was a kickstarter stretch goal, is essential to me keeping this one in our collection. The normal board is not nearly as good.
text_fidelity_b: Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers

text_fidelity_a: Lifetime Geometric Dome Climber Play Center (Primary Colors), 60-Inch I was looking for some play equipment for my 4 year old since our new house doesn't have a playground in walking distance. I eyed this for months before finally deciding to go ahead and order it from another site where I found a lower price due to a coupon I had. I was surprised at the small size of the box. Assembly was fairly easy but took a few hours. Once the pattern is established, it is pretty self explanatory. I was very impressed with this when completed. The handles are like rock wall handles and great for kids who need more to grip. My 4 year old is now scaling this thing with no problem. A month in, I don't see any signs of wear. The color is nice because it blends into the landscape. Pulling through the neighborhood, it doesn't stand out like an eyesore. We have this and the matching small swingset from lifetime. I would recommend Lifetime's products to anyone. This feels commercial weight. We have it placed above a bed of thick mulch to cushion falls, but it is also easy to move if we need to place it somewhere else in the yard.  For the price, you can't beat it.

text_fidelity_a: Kiddieland Mickey Deluxe Trike, Ride on My toddler is really into Mickey right now so I just had to get him this trike. It’s adorable and super well made. Assembly was straightforward, thanks to clear and helpful instructions. It took me about half an hour to put together but my toddler was “helping” me so it really wouldn’t take quite that long. I really appreciate the design of this trike since it’s made to grow with your child. It starts out with safety straps, bars that lock in as a secondary way to keep your child in the seat and a handle so you can push and steer. There’s a switch on the front wheel that you slide so it will move without the pedals. Once your child gets big enough to ride alone, move the switch back and the front wheel is controlled by the pedals. The handle is removable as are the safety bars and canopy. I always love finding toys that will get a lot of use since there are so many things that are really only made for short time periods or specific developmental stages then they’re quickly outgrown. This is a wonderful toy and I’m looking forward to helping my son learn to ride it as he grows.
text_fidelity_b: Kiddieland Mickey Deluxe Trike, Ride on

When a card is turned over that matches their chosen "moustache", they slam it down on the card, causing the attached suction cup to attach to that card.

It's a great memory game! If the player smashes the wrong card, they lose 2 of their winning cards. Each player has to remember which one(style and color) they have under their nose. It's also great for motor skills, since they have to aim for the card, possibly in a race against another person.

I was pleasantly surprised at how sturdy the "moustaches" actually are. (The handles remind me of a kitchen spoon/spatula handle.) The "moustaches" are larger than I expected and they're a sturdy rubber material. There are 6 different shapes/styles in 3 different colors(black, yellow, and brown).

I've had lots of fun playing this game with my newly 6 year old(delayed) and my 3 year old. My 19 month old has had fun, too, but he doesn't play by the rules. ;) This is a great game for some family fun. Laughs are pretty much guaranteed!

text_fidelity_a:
Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange This is a simple "flick-and-write" game with good production values, a questionable rulebook, simple and fast gameplay, and a box that is just ridiculously large for what it is.

Gameplay is fast and straightforward, involving a Crokinole style mechanism for shooting your disc into a recessed game board with a central hole in the middle. This board has a plastic shelf with corner sections for "shooting" pieces, and they'll fall into a central area divided into four main sections. My central board easily comes loose from the shelving piece, and needs to be adjusted prior to gameplay almost all the time. Once you shoot, you'll be making marks onto your player board with the included markers, which are of average quality for a game like this. The boards are easily erasable - a major plus to the production aspect of the game.

The rules are not that hard, but they are explained in a way that makes learning the game quite a bit more difficult than it needs to be. Few examples are covered, and there will be a number of times that you run into situations where you aren't sure how to interpret the rule as written. Once you get it though, play is not too hard, and Sonora is something you can play with the kids after you've worked out the kinks. And they'll want to play this - it's colorful, with kid-friendly artwork, and the gameplay looks like a kid's game, but has enough meat to interest an adult for at least a little while. I don't know that I'd play this game too often, but it is certainly different and a good family game that will keep kids interested. You can play a few games back to back, as they'll run 20 minutes or so once you know the general flow of the game. For a family game night, this will be a good alternative to a more traditional strategy or roll-and-move board game.

The biggest downfall of this one is that the box is so large. As a gamer with a large collection, it's disappointing to see a 12x12 "Ticket to Ride" sized box for a game that could have opted for a foldable game board and fit into a very small game box. Even if they must have a one-piece board, dropping the molded plastic insert that holds a handful of discs and pens could have reduced the size by a few inches in depth. In reality, there's not much here in the box, and the components can be entirely stored in the recessed game board area alone. That would be about 3/4" in depth, not 3".

All in all, it's OK.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO NINJAGO Temple of Resurrection 70643 Building Kit (765 Piece) What I like with this LEGO set is that it does come with 7 mini figures. Makes it so much easier for me because I didn't have to run out to try to find some type of figures so the kids were able to play with this once they got it all built.
I let the older grandchildren go ahead and build this by themselves. It's getting hard for Paps to see all those smaller pieces anymore.
What was cute is that once they had it about 1/2 way built, they let the smaller kids pretend that the "warriors" were in command on getting their temple built. Because of that, they really helped keep the younger ones occupied for at least 3 days.
This is what I love about toys like this. Kids aren't glued to the tv, and kids aren't glued to their phones. They are using their brains and their hands to build something. Then they are using their brains to come up with a new adventure each time they play with it.
And, it's not set for just one age group. Yes, to build it the child has to be a certain age to understand the concept of putting it all together and reading the instructions. But, once it's all built the younger children (once they know not to put small items in their mouths or destroy what's built) can join in and play. Right now we have kids ranging from 4 1/2 to 12 playing with it. And when they grow older and lose interest in it, we pack up the entire set in zip baggies, add the instructions, and repack it into the box to save for the next generation of kids in the future.
I have always liked how well LEGOS are made. Parts are nice and sturdy and the colors on the blocks seem to last for years on end.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO NINJAGO Temple of Resurrection 70643 Building Kit (765 Piece)

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Horse Club 70-Piece Lakeside Country Dollhouse and Horse Stable Playset for Kids Ages 5-12 This box was heavy!
The quality of the pieces is exceptional.
The house and barn come together quickly and easily. They click together and they can easily be separated by pushing on the tabs if you wanted to take it apart.
I cannot attest to the durability of the horses legs, which were packaged with cardboard between them, which worried me that they might be fragile. Time will tell on that.
But the structure itself is very stable. There are SO MANY accessories. The house has specific locations where the picture sticker is added to the wall and the ribbons get added to the wall, etc.
I was surprised by the amount of details.
I love the attic hatch in the floor and the telescope in the attic. The only thing I think it is missing is a third person. The family photo that comes with it has four people in the family. The bedrooms can fit four people. Also, I do wish that all the people could ride the horses and not just the one person.
It would be nice if two people were included that could ride a horse so it would be easier to have so siblings or friends play together. The saddle is elaborate.
My 10 year old niece thought this was really neat and was excited to play with it.
My almost 5 year old nephews were excited to play with it also, they like to play with the farm set that is at a 1:64th scale, I was kind of expecting these to be at that scale, but it is much bigger.
Schleich is very high quality brand for miniatures and has a good reputation for that reason.
I guess I'll have to buy a few more kits to get a rider and another kid for the family.

PRO’s: width and length of slide (twice as long as other slides in target audience), easy setup/operate/put away, splash zone (pool at end) works to stop toddlers. CON’s: the streaming water that “wets” the slide is too wide near the end of the slide and hardly existing at the start of the slide. A simple design improvement would be to have far less watering holes for the slip and slide near the splash zone and progressively more as you near the starting point. This to be is the largest flaw in the slide.
There are ways to “work around” the lack of water on the slide (the lack of slipperiness) but the product should fix this vs the customer having workarounds.

My Critter Catcher - Spider and Insect Catcher So I know that spiders are generally good, in that they eat other bugs. But they are also terrifying because they are FAST and HIDE BEHIND THINGS, just waiting to attack! Trying to remove them with a cup and piece of paper is perilous at best (what if it GETS OUT and gets on my hand?? I would flail in terror and then who knows where it would land?). So, to defend myself from these miniature terrors, I bought this.

I knew my time had come when my cats were staring at the floor. It was my nemesis, a spider. I tore the catcher out of the packaging and - with only a little shrieking - successfully subdued the spider! It was caught in the bristles, unable to escape! And I was at a safe distance, unlike the cup method where I'd be practically touching the spider. I darted outside and released it. I told the spider he was evicted and to eat bugs outside, never inside. If it ever does venture inside aagin, I know my cat sentries would alert me to its presence and - with minimal shrieking - I could safely evict it again.
text_fidelity_b: My Critter Catcher - Spider and Insect Catcher

text_fidelity_a: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster The recon has always been a pretty good blaster.  Somewhat prone to jamming, and on the short side for range, but accurate as all get out, and good for modding.  Then enter the Retaliator!  This is not your typical Recon with a face lift!  The shell is still recon- but with a new name badge and the digital camo effect.  The GUTS are all new- direct plunger powerhouse.  This blaster will pop the elite darts out to 75 feet (angled shots) and will put darts out to 50 feet level shot.  The accuracy is still there too!  It will take the old Streamlines too(with a noticable loss of range and accuracy)  This blaster will jam- but if your careful to pull the cocking slide back fully (not just till it clicks, but fully back, usually a couple mm beyond the point of the trigger latch engagment) jams are minimal (we actully shot 50 or so shots without a jam!).  I'm not a huge fan of barrel and stock attachments, but these are pretty good on this blaster.  The barrel does reduce range (about 8 to 10 foot lose), but does increase accuracy (we use cardboard standups aprox 2" wide by 4" high and can hit them 8 out of 10 time without the barrel and 9 out of 10 with- at 25 feet).  The new 12 shot clip (mag) is very cool and makes a nice transition between the 6 shot (way to small) and the 18 (nice capacity- but kinda gets in the way).  My daughter uses this blaster to sniper me all the time.  All she needs to see is a foot or a hand sticking out from behind the couch and I'm toast!  All in all a worthy upgrade to the recon.  Great for a primary or secondary carry.  I did take 1 star off because nerf still hasn't made this jam proof- close, but not perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Swim Center Family Inflatable Pool, 120" X 72" X 22", for Ages 6+ We purchased this pool together with the following products:

- Intex The Wet Set Rectangular Pool Cover
- Intex 120V AC Quickfill Pump
- 10'X12' HD Tarp
- Associated pool toys

Set up was made quick and easy by matching the large opening on the pump with each of the three large intake openings on the pool to get all three levels quickly filled with air, starting at the bottom as per the directions. After laying out the tarp the pool unfolded quickly and we centered it over the tarp prior to inflating. We followed the suggestions of other reviewers to use the smaller tip on the pump with the smaller valve openings on the pool to finalize the air fill so as not to over inflate. The entire setup process couldn't have taken more than 15-20 minutes. Very easy.

It took another 20-25 minutes to fill the pool with a garden hose to the fill line clearly marked inside the pool. With a 90 degree day outside in the sun we could have done without adding any hot water but we did put in a couple pots anyway. We also added a cup of household bleach to the pool as one reviewer suggested. Undoubtedly there are better ways of keeping the water clean and we'll research those as we go along. We simply wanted to get up and running quickly the first time as our 5 year old couldn't wait.

Wouldn't have set this pool up any other way. The electric air pump made inflation of the three levels very quick and easy. I would recommend a tarp (they're quite inexpensive at Lowes or Home Depot), and while you could use a bed sheet as a pool cover we're quite satisfied with the Intex product.

Just a reminder - there's a single drain valve in the bottom corner of the pool. Remember to close that prior to filling. I forgot to do it and as I began filling the pool I thought it had arrived with a leak. Doh!

Keep in mind that this is a day 1 review. Cleaning, etc., may dampen our enthusiasm but if this pool lasts through the summer it will have been well worth the investment.

The only complaint we have after our first really fun day with this pool is that Amazon lowered the price by $5 the day after ours arrived. That's the second time this has happened to us with an Amazon purchase. While it's only $5 it is irksome.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Swim Center Family Inflatable Pool, 120" X 72" X 22", for Ages 6+

ThinkFun and Crazy Aaron's Thinking Putty Puzzle and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Ages 8 and Up - The Famous Thinking Putty in Logic Game Form I’ve played many of Thinkfun’s logic puzzles, and use them in my classroom. So, I was very interested in their new logic puzzle that uses Crazy Aaron’s Putty. This game has some similarities with their other logic puzzles. It comes with 60 cards that show the challenge setup on one side and a possible answer on the back. The setup for each challenge takes the longest than any other logic puzzle because you have to tear the balls of putty off each color. It is challenging, even the first few challenges’ solutions aren’t immediately visible, they take some thought to solve.

I enjoyed this for myself and found it relaxing to put together and solve. I could see some kids not having the patience to play through the puzzle. I don’t plan to use this one in my classroom because I think the putty would get funky after having some kids play with it, and there could be some putty mixing that intentionally or unintentionally could happen and ruin the game.

Overall, this is a very clever idea. I’ve played the beginning challenges and enjoyed figuring them out. Kids will love the putty, but I’m not sure how long the challenges will hold their attention.

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll Since the first Barbie doll was created in 1959, little girl's have always loved to style/color Barbie doll's hair, and this fun to color hair Barbie is no exception. (I took my 1960's ponytail down, so she could look like Sleeping Beauty back in the day!) This gorgeous Color Stylin' Hair Barbie is a huge favorite with the grandchildren now.

Barbie comes with a suction cupped chair, comb, applicator brush, bowl, seven color swatches in 3 colors-3 pink, 2 purple and 2 orange, clip on foiler holder and rubberbands. Barbie is dressed in a glittery pink dress with shoes, necklace and belt. The color application is easy- seat Barbie in her chair, which doesn't move due to an ingenious suction cup bottom, wet the hair section you want to color, place the color swatch in the foiler, then clip the foiler to the wet hair and pull through. When you want to remove the color or color again, you just wash and dry the hair and you are ready for more fun.

There are a couple things you should know before using this coloring set: don't color near carpet, furniture, walls or clothes you don't want to ruin, as these colors can be a permanent stain for certain fabrics or walls. I laid down a cheap plastic tablecloth from the dollar store, so the girls had a great area to play on with no worries. I called Mattel, and found they do not sell extra color swatches, so once these are used up, they are gone, and to replace the colors, you would have to buy another doll. This is a shame, as they always sell accessories and extra hair swatches for the dolls with hair swatches that can be cut, so why not some inexpensive color swatches too Mattel?

The girls just love coloring, braiding and styling the gorgeous streaked areas of this Barbie's hair, so of course they want more colors- and even different colors too. As for something interesting I noticed, I bought another one of these dolls, as I have 2 granddaughters, and we immediately noticed one set colored darkly and another set colored very faintly. I looked closely at the boxes and what did I find on the backs of the boxes, but an expiration date! It says Best Used By and then a date which you need a magnifying glass to read. Reading the back of our boxes showed that one of the boxes colors was expired! That explains the faint color! Being a wonderfully fun to play with Barbie gives this doll 5 Stars, but color that is expired and having no refills brings her down to limited playability with the color, making this gorgeous Barbie a 4 Star doll.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll

text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:58af1484fac2632df11b3d8e403acedc]] Addendum: Two years old now and these toys are still working great and popular with the kids. I assume the ease of filling in the pool and the ability to shoot whatever they want without getting fussed at adds to their appeal.

I got both the Matchbox Aqua Cannon Swamp Blaster and this Fire Truck Rig for 5 and 6 year old grandkids. Until I showed them how to use the toys, they didn't show much interest in them. Once the trucks were filled and squirting, however, they happily shot at their sister for about 15 minutes. It didn't keep their interest long but there were enough kids to share the toys that they stayed in action for an hour or so.

They toys fill easily and are easy to load and shoot. We submerged the trucks in the pool so that they self-filled meaning that only the kids were only limited by their ability to keep pumping (see photo).

I find these a great alternative to water guns. The volume and strength of the shots are less than those oversized guns but enough to shoot all the way across the pool. Because they are not guns, the kids are less likely to feel the need to aim them at people.

I think these toys are best suited for ages five and under.

1 year followup: This toy spent the winter outside by the pool and it still works like new. I have to keep it out of the hands of adults who delight in shooting water far outside the pool area (violating house rules).
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

It’s worth mentioning that the overall set is a bit smaller than anticipated, so I’ve used a standard pencil in my photos for a size comparison. Regardless, it’s still appropriate for the recommended ages of 3-6. I didn’t notice any off-putting scent, but there is a mild fresh wood smell, which is to be expected. The nob on top doesn't make any loud sounds when rotating it, and the whisk portion is actually a little bit flexible due to the string construction in the center. I think all of the pieces have a genuine purpose in this set, and the features function nicely, but I do feel the cookie design is a missed opportunity. It would have been very creative for one side of each cookie to represent the unbaked cookie, and the opposite side could have been decorated with a fun icing color or sprinkles, just to add a pop of color and give a start-to-finish concept (maybe a future craft project for us). text_fidelity_a:
Little Tikes Pillow Racers Fire Truck My boys love this thing! They are 1(average for age) and 4(very small), but they are about the same size. It's the perfect size for both of them, but it is on the small size. I don't think it will be too long before they get too big for it. Of course, another little will be right behind them to give it more use!

They have so much fun with it, of course I recommend it. But, there are a few MINOR negative issues I have with it.

-Keep the instructions initially! Getting that handle attached is more difficult than it would seem. Also, you want to have some strong hands close by to push in the wheels. It was extremely hard for me to get them to pop in. I do admit my hands are pretty weak, and I am an exhausted pregnant momma. The average person might not have trouble with them, but I'd be on the safe side. :)

-There are little velcro strips on the bottom that is suppose to keep the cloth in place. It doesn't work for us. It keeps coming loose as the boys play, and we have to constantly reattach it. Thankfully, it's not long enough to drag the floor too bad, so it doesn't create a tripping hazard.

-My boys do tip off the back a good bit while riding. Since it's so small, it has never caused them harm. They jump back up and keep playing. I do think it surprised them the first couple of times, but they are used to it by now. It might not be the best toy for really young children just learning coordination, though.

Overall, despite my small complaints, I still think this is a great toy that will provide lots of fun!
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Pillow Racers Fire Truck

text_fidelity_a:
Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.
text_fidelity_b: Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA

A way better experience than just kids watching videos in the backseat, and parents listening to the radio in front.

Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition Werewolf is not usually a "game night" game that you play with a group of friends. I've always used it in classroom settings, or with larger groups, usually upwards of 10 people, where this game really shines. Ultimately, Werewolf is a deduction game in which most players are Villagers, unwittingly being killed or eliminated by a sect of Werewolf players. Using very limited clues and knowledge, it's up to the Villagers to unmask the Werewolves and eliminate them from the game before they themselves are eaten.

The only real issue that I have with Werewolf is that there is player elimination, although since Werewolf is not a particularly long game, it's usually OK, and bystanders often have as much fun as the players.

There are plenty of versions of this game available out there, but I think that Bezier's "Ultimate" is certainly the way to go. The bits are durable and well made, and there are enough cards to play an 80 person game. That said, there is less content in here as compared to the "Revised Edition" that came out a few years ago. I still think that this is the box to get, however, as the roles and unique playing styles presented in the "Revised" box are more complicated, and not really in line with the casual spirit of the game. I think they certainly provide more variety, but at the expense of complicating the players and making it far more difficult for the moderator. As it's impossible to answer questions mid-game, it's best to leave the complicated roles to a different genre of game.

A 5-Star Product for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition

Elefun and Friends Barrel of Monkeys Game - Colors May Vary Ok. Here's the deal. If you actually order and receive the Elefun version produced with/through Hasbro as the current item listed as of this date shows, here's the real review by an adult:

There are 10 monkeys in a barrel. It is listed on the plastic, throw away wrapping. And that's what you get from this brand. 10. Each barrel has ten color corresponding monkeys.
About the monkeys: they are durable and not flimsy. The monkey's tails are part of the body and are not useable. All monkeys are the same mold.....BUT there are 2 each of different facial expressions. This is not so easy to notice while playing but yes, the monkeys are in facial pairs. All monkeys are the same size.

Now.....lol....from a serious player (lol) that grew up with the 60s, 70s versions: these monkeys have....two arms....one arm is bent closer to the head so it's open loop is a tad smaller. Meaning....it makes a differnece in how easy or hard it is to link them. Also....the hand shape....well....it isn't as pointed and hook like as it was years ago. So yes....it is harder and I think that's a reason there is only 10 now.

Is it fun? Yes. Worth the money?? To me....because a fast food meal costs this much. And replayablity is very high. Also....you can buy two and do color challenges. Or time two players....or lots of creativity to play.

I would rather have a reproduction of the original. BUT these are functional and in my honest review, more difficult to chain over 7; making for more competition.

I think this is a good product for children, teens, families and elderly.

**I also think this could help anyone with motor skill issues or be good for even Alzheimer persons who enjoy things simple and close up.

This is a good product.
text_fidelity_b: Elefun and Friends Barrel of Monkeys Game - Colors May Vary

text_fidelity_a: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32" Purchased one of these without exactly knowing what I was buying. Sure, I knew it made noise - but didn't know how it did that or what it might sound like ( guess I could have looked on YouTube, but I didn't). Anyway, now that I've got one it's all everyone wants to play with. Basically it's a short tube with a thin piece of taut plastic covering one end (think tiny drum head), and a long loose spring mounted to the center of the plastic. Holding the tube and shaking it causes the spring to vibrate like springs do, those vibrations travel up to the drum head and the sound reverberates into the tube and is amplified out the other end. Makes for some pretty interesting sound effects. Overall I'm more than happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32"

Cheerson CX-10 Mini 29mm Diameter 4CH 2.4GHz 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter UFO RTF Green I would recommend this drone as anyone's first drone, or as a cheap toy to keep in the office.

I've purchased several of these for the children in my family. The are small, light, and perfect for flying indoors. I've crashed mine several time from 8-10 feet up and they just fall about bounce off the ground. The basic-ness of this drone reinforces the skills needed to fly all drones at a very low entry cost. In this way you don't feel bad about trying things and crashing. The features are very basic with the only programmed/smart option is a flip. There is a sort of hidden option to unlock "acrobatic mode" (read the instructions to unlock) which is really just turning the sensitivity of the controller, but definitely a challenge for new flyers.

Once you master flying this little guy around jumping up to a bigger "smarter" drone is a piece of cake, and if anything goes wrong you have the fundamental skills to fly and land.
